qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Ferrari commands an exceptional luxury brand intangible moat and supreme pricing power, but on a look-through portfolio basis the asset base is heavily weighted toward cyclical automotive and industrial price-takers (Stellantis, CNH Industrial, Iveco, Philips) that suffer margin erosion and fail the 12% multi-cycle ROIC bar.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Reject). While Ferrari (~35-45% of GAV) is an unassailable ultra-luxury franchise, Exor's look-through economics are heavily exposed to mass automotive manufacturing (Stellantis) and cyclical agricultural/construction machinery (CNH Industrial). These holdings lack pricing power over the full cycle, suffer severe competitive and EV transition headwinds, and fail the 12% ROIC hurdle.
qualitative.evidence: Stellantis faces significant margin compression, inventory gluts, and price cutting amidst structural EV transition pressure. CNH Industrial and Iveco are capital-intensive cyclical machinery manufacturers. Look-through ROIC across the non-Ferrari portfolio remains well below the cost of capital, precluding a Quality pass under the look-through holding company standard.
